newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on market liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on market liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 40 basis points at 20.80 percent on Monday due to ample market liquidity, traders said.
"It was not a very active session, but the market still feels very liquid, and in fact we expect primary rates to fall again tomorrow," a trader said.
Traders added that a stable peso and low secondary market rates set the stage for further cuts in primary rates at Tuesday's weekly central bank auction of government securities.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended down 45 basis points at 21.90 percent.
Dealers said bellwether 28-day Cetes rates could fall by 25-50 basis points at Tuesday's primary placement from last week's assignment rate of 21.45 percent.

Stable U.S. long bond yields were also conducive to falls in domestic primary rates, traders said. Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds stood at 6.70 percent in late trade on Monday, compared to 6.71 percent on Friday.
Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity in the market by draining 4.207 billion pesos.
Liquidity of just 307 million pesos was scheduled to return to the market on Tuesday, but traders said total liquidity could well increase during the session due to more government spending.
